name: MOTS-c

lead: MOTS-c is a short peptide encoded in mitochondrial DNA, first described in 2015. It is sold as a research chemical.

In mouse studies it improved insulin sensitivity and metabolic health, and it is promoted for fat loss, endurance and longevity. Human evidence is limited mainly to observational data and early-phase work on analogs.

paras: MOTS-c is reported to act on the folate-methionine cycle and activate AMPK, shifting cellular metabolism, and may move to the nucleus under stress to regulate gene expression.
Human safety data are essentially absent for vendor products. It is not an approved drug and is prohibited by anti-doping agencies; purity and identity of gray-market peptides are unreliable.
